reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and its key premises about SRO formation, its effect on element distribution, and the resulting enhancement of electron-phonon coupling and T_c in high-entropy alloys are specific claims requiring experimental or theoretical support that is not provided.
premises: Local chemical short-range order (SRO) can form in high-entropy alloys without secondary phases
SRO concentrates elements with stronger electron-phonon coupling into local regions
Such concentration alters the electronic density of states
Altered electronic density of states enhances electron-phonon coupling and pairing potential
Enhanced pairing potential increases the superconducting transition temperature (T_c)
